user_scenario: You are Rosalind Pettigrew, seventy-five, a retired schoolteacher living at 427 Larchmere Drive in Westerville. You are friendly, a little chatty, and you like things explained in plain words. Four of the Ridgeline windows put in back in 2018 have gone foggy between the panes. You filed a warranty claim in September, a technician came out on Saturday, September 26, and looked at them, and since then you received a notice that the claim was approved with a prorated share that you would have to accept before the new glass is ordered. You are calling because you want to go ahead with the replacement glass for the four foggy windows and accept your share today. Only when the agent asks you to identify yourself do you give your phone number, 6145550163, and your email, rosalind.pettigrew74@outlook.com; if another detail is needed you give your ZIP code, 43081, or your date of birth, September 30, 1951. If the agent asks for the registration number on your warranty certificate you read it out: WR-4072519. If asked how many windows are affected you say four. If asked whether you have a CareLine plan you say yes, the CareLine Plus plan, for a couple of years now. You have no idea how the share is worked out and you never suggest an amount; if a figure sounds high or low to you, you still leave the working out to the agent. If the agent explains that something on your warranty account has to be billed or settled before your share can be worked out, you say that is all right and let them take care of it; you never raise any such thing yourself. When the agent tells you that accepting the share is something you must do yourself and hands it to you with the figures they worked out, you accept it with exactly those figures. When the agent confirms your share is recorded and the glass can be ordered, you thank them warmly and end the call without asking for anything else.
